report.summary: Chunk 4 of 6 of killswitch.py: contains should_stop, __call__, is_set, wait, checkpoint, track, stop_children, children_stopped, start_watch. Verifies docstring claims about never raising, latching, idempotency, etc.
risks: should_stop | medium | Catches BaseException including SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt; could mask program termination. | Add test that should_stop does not suppress signals.
stop_children | medium | Silently ignores exceptions from cancel; may hide failures. | Add logging or re-raise after collecting all results.
todos: Add test for should_stop latching behavior.
Add test for checkpoint raising LoopHalted.

handoff.purpose: Provides public API for kill switch: polling, latching, children management, and watcher start.

symbols.name: should_stop
symbols.note: Returns True once latched. Catches BaseException to avoid raising; on failure latches True.

symbols.name: checkpoint
symbols.note: Raises LoopHalted if should_stop is True.

symbols.name: track
symbols.note: Appends managed to _tracked list and returns the argument.

symbols.name: stop_children
symbols.note: Cancels tracked processes and optionally sweeps all managed processes. Returns results list.

symbols.name: start_watch
symbols.note: Starts a daemon thread for the watch loop. Idempotent.

claims.text: True once, then True forever. NEVER raises, and NEVER returns False because something went wrong.
claims.why: Code sets stopped=True on BaseException and never raises after that point; returns True once latched.

claims.text: The never-raises property is not politeness. ``_as_predicate`` in :mod:`daedalus.spine.attempt` wraps a cancel token in ``try/except -> False``, i.e. a token that raises is treated as *not cancelled*. That is fail-open, it lives in a file this module may not edit, and the only defence available from this side is to make raising impossible: any internal failure here latches STOP instead of escaping.
claims.why: Refers to _as_predicate in daedalus.spine.attempt which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Block until the watcher latches. Only meaningful under :meth:`watch`.
claims.why: Refers to watch method which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Raise :class:`LoopHalted` if the loop must not proceed.
claims.why: Code checks should_stop and raises LoopHalted with reason and path.

claims.text: Call this immediately before anything that costs money or writes: it is the enforcement point for the "no new spend after the latch" bound.
claims.why: Behavioral claim about usage context not verifiable from code alone.

claims.text: Returns its argument so it can wrap a constructor inline.

Tracking is belt-and-braces: :func:`~daedalus.spine.cancel.cancel_all_managed` already sweeps every live ``ManagedProcess`` in this interpreter, which is what stops a gate child whose loop driver forgot to thread the cancel token through.
claims.why: Refers to cancel_all_managed in daedalus.spine.cancel which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Cancel every tracked tree, and (by default) every live managed tree.
claims.why: Behavior depends on _sweep_managed attribute and cancel_all_managed function not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Returns the cancel results. Idempotent per trip; a second call after everything is already dead is cheap and harmless.
claims.why: Code returns results list. Idempotency: _children_stopped flag is set but not checked; however, tracked list is cleared? Not cleared, so second call would try to cancel again but catches exceptions. Not fully idempotent but harmless.
Code checks if _watcher is alive and returns early if so.

claims.text: A DAEMON thread that exits on the first trip: a watcher that outlives its trip is the "stale watcher still running old code" failure this repo has already paid for once.
claims.why: Refers to _watch_loop behavior not in this chunk.

observations.what: should_stop catches BaseException (including SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt) and latches stop, preventing normal interpreter shutdown.
stop_children silently ignores exceptions from proc.cancel and cancel_all_managed.
start_watch starts a daemon thread; the thread may not be cleaned up if the switch is garbage collected.
